newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEEK SOFTER ON PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEEK SOFTER ON PRESSURE.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar finished the week on Friday easier against hard currencies on the back of slight import pressure, dealers said.

"There was some import pressure and the dollar went on depreciating until it hit 10.6800/7000 -- some guys were evening quoting 10.6850/7050. Then the Reserve Bank came in and dumped a few (U.S.) dollars into the market," a dealer said.
The local unit ended the day at 10.6750/6950 against the U.S. money, down from it's Thursday close of 10.6400/6600.
It was also quoted weaker against pound sterling at 17.7900/8100 compared to 17.7100/7300, tracking in part an easier U.S. dollar overseas and was at 7.0900/1100 from 7.0600/0800 versus the mark.
Against South Africa's rand, the Zimbabwe dollar closed at 2.2800/3000, two cents down from 2.2600/2800 the previous day. --Stella Mapenzauswa, Harare Newsroom: +263-4 72 52 28/9--
